subject: CascadeCare discovery — SLOs, model fit, and next technical steps
content:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@cascadecare.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + confirmation of priorities from today's discovery

Thanks for the call earlier — quick note to capture what mattered to us and make sure we're aligned on asks and success metrics before the technical deep dive. High-level items from our side: 

- Business pain: Current latency spikes on our QA help assistant are driving abandonment during high traffic windows (especially 10:00–14:00 ET).
- Primary goal: Move to a predictable 95th percentile response time under 200ms for short instruction prompts (<= 256 tokens) while keeping per-token cost in line with our budget.
- Volume profile: baseline 450 req/s, burst to ~1,200 req/s (peaks last 20–30 minutes).
- Security: must run in a private VPC with customer-managed KMS; SOC2 evidence and audit logs required.

Appreciate if you can summarize the technical approach you'll propose (model candidate, topology, cost/throughput assumptions) and a suggested mutual action plan. Also attaching our usage snapshot (anonymized).

— Liam
Head of Platform Engineering
CascadeCare

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@cascadecare.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + confirmation of priorities from today's discovery

Liam — thanks, this is helpful and matches what we heard on the call. Below is a concise recap and the technical follow-up items we'll own before next week.

Recap of pain & goals (short):
- Latency: p95 target <= 200ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens).
- Throughput: steady 450 req/s, required burst capacity ~1,200 req/s.
- Security: Private VPC deployment with customer KMS + audit logs.
- Cost sensitivity: prioritize a topology/path that minimizes per-token spend while meeting p95.

Initial technical proposal (high level):
1) Model candidates: instruction-tuned 13B and 70B open models for tiered routing. 13B (quantized 4-bit) as primary for most requests; 70B for long-form/high-quality responses or fallbacks.
2) Hardware/topology: Dedicated pool in us-west-2 with mixed-instance serving: 6x A100-80GB for steady-state + 2x burst nodes (A100 or H100) for peaks. Autoscaler configured to add burst nodes when queue latency > 40ms for 2 consecutive seconds.
3) Batching & cache: Request routing to use small dynamic batching (batch sizes 8–32 depending on latency headroom) and prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts (we observed 28% repeat prefix rate in the snapshot).
4) SLO enforcement & fallback: Primary route to quantized 13B with p95 guardrails; automated fallback to a smaller low-latency variant on capacity constraints and a degrade plan to return cached answers for specific queries if model capacity exhausted.
5) Security & compliance: Private control plane + VPC peering; we'll provide SOC2 artifacts and a KMS integration plan.

Deliverables we will send by Tuesday:
- A draft SLO-runbook with p95/p99 budgets and measured estimates (latency and token cost).
- Deployment topology sketch (pdf) with autoscaling knobs and estimated GPU footprint.
- Mutual action plan (owner + dates).

Next steps (quick):
- We will prepare the SLO spreadsheet and the topology sketch and share by EOD Tuesday.
- Please confirm which model output quality thresholds matter (e.g., 1–3 quantitative eval metrics or example prompts you care about).

I'll loop in Marissa for the deeper latency/throughput numbers.

Thanks,
David Kim
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@cascadecare.com>, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + confirmation of priorities from today's discovery

Liam — following up with a technical deep-dive note and concrete numbers based on the usage snapshot you shared. Key assumptions and estimates below.

Workload assumptions derived from snapshot:
- Median prompt tokens: 60 tokens; 95th prompt tokens: 420 tokens.
- Interaction pattern: 72% single-turn, 28% multi-turn where KV cache helps.

Latency math (p95 target <= 200ms for <=256 tokens):
- Inference latency components: model forward + token decode + RPC/queueing. For quantized 13B on A100-80GB with optimized kernels we estimate: forward+decode ~ 35–55ms for <=256 tokens (batch size 16), queueing tail depends on concurrency.
- To meet p95 <= 200ms at 1,200 req/s burst we recommend dynamic sharding across 6 steady nodes (optimistic) with 2 burst nodes. Estimated concurrency per node: 150–250 concurrent small requests depending on batching efficiency.

Throughput & capacity estimate (rough):
- Steady 450 req/s: 6x A100-80GB (13B quantized) comfortably handles baseline with headroom for batching.
- Burst to 1,200 req/s: +2 burst nodes to reduce queueing; autoscale threshold set by sustained 30s over baseline.
- If you need stricter p99 latency, we will recommend extra headroom (1–2 additional steady nodes) or more aggressive packing with lower batch sizes.

Model accuracy / quality tradeoffs:
- 13B quantized (4-bit) gives good latency/cost with acceptable quality for most help-assistant queries. We propose a small eval suite from your examples (you mentioned ten representative queries) to validate.
- 70B (float16) reserved for long-form or high-accuracy paths — routed by intent classifier in the proxy layer.

Security & topology notes:
- Private VPC deployment model: control plane in Redwood-hosted account with private connectivity; inference fleet deployed into your VPC via customer-submitted AMIs (or our on-prem package). KMS wrap for model keys and audit log forwarding to your SIEM.

Operational runbook highlights (what we'll submit):
- Canary steps for rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48–72 hours) with automatic rollback triggers on p95/regression in eval metrics.
- Cost controls: token caps, model routing policies, and quantization profiles per route.

Attachments: draft SLO spreadsheet and a topology sketch attached.

Proposed immediate MAP items (owner — due):
- Send 10 eval prompts and preferred quality criteria — Liam — Mon 6/26
- Review draft SLO spreadsheet and add business tolerance bands — Priya — Tue 6/27
- Review VPC/KMS onboarding checklist — CascadeCare infra — Thu 6/29

If that aligns, we'll lock estimates and prepare a short cost/latency tradeoff sheet for the two model options.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
